fix: Open the container in Tag Manager and look at the tags the finding names and their triggers. Where a tracker is not needed on this page, change its trigger so it does not fire here, or remove it. For the question of whether a tracker is allowed here, the client should ask their own counsel.
tech: Only with --trackers, on the pages the first check counts. The container's public file (GET www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=GTM-XXXX, the file every visitor receives) is read as text, once per container, at most three per page, and never run; its escaped characters are decoded and the same table of patterns is applied, with Google Analytics 4's measurement id read from a tag's settings. What the file holds is what the container could load: whether a tag fires on this page depends on its triggers, which Gaugeline does not run, and the finding says so. A tag built from a template that keeps its id out of the file is not seen. A container that cannot be read, or is longer than the size cap, is could-not-check with the reason
done: The client has seen what each Tag Manager container on this page holds and has decided with their own counsel which tags stay; running Gaugeline again shows the list they chose.
estimateChanges: An hour in the Tag Manager workspace per container, with the client. More when tags are built from templates and the triggers are long.

title: On the website, not in fulfillment
what: A product on your website has no matching product in Printful.
why: For something you print, nobody will make the order. For a ticket, a download or a service, that is expected and nothing needs fixing.
fix: If the product should be printed, create it in Printful or save its Printful id on the website product. Otherwise leave it.
tech: a published Sanity product that matchProducts paired with no Printful product; runs only when both Sanity and Printful returned data; low because most shops sell some products that are not printed; one finding per product with its name and id
done: The product exists in Printful and is linked by id, or is left as website-only on purpose.
estimateChanges: Setting up artwork and variants in Printful if the product is new there.

title: In fulfillment, not on the website
what: A Printful product is not linked to any product on your website.
why: It is probably a sample, a draft or a product that was taken off the website. It can still be ordered through Printful's own store.
fix: Delete it in Printful if it is a leftover, or save its id on the website product it belongs to.
tech: a Printful product in matchProducts' unmatchedPrintful; runs only when both Sanity and Printful returned data; one finding per product with its name and id
done: The leftover is deleted in Printful, or its id is saved on the website product it belongs to.
estimateChanges: Checking nothing still sells from it.

title: In checkout, not on the website
what: An active Stripe product is not linked to any product on your website.
why: It may be a payment link or an invoice item on purpose. If it is a leftover, it clutters reports and someone may sell it by mistake.
fix: If it is meant to exist, leave it. If not, archive it in Stripe, or save its id on the website product it belongs to.
tech: an active Stripe product in matchProducts' unmatchedStripe; archived ones are skipped; runs only when both Sanity and Stripe returned data, because with no website products read every Stripe product would be unmatched; one finding per product with its name and id
done: The product is left as meant, archived, or linked by id to its website product.
estimateChanges: Subscriptions on it need care before it is archived.

title: A price is stored in two systems
what: The same price is saved on the Sanity product and on the matched Stripe product, and the two agree today.
why: Two copies that agree today are the cause of next month's mismatch: the next price change has to be made twice, and one of them will be forgotten.
fix: Decide which system owns each price, usually checkout, and have the other read it instead of storing its own copy.
tech: a Sanity product with a price whose matched Stripe product has a default price with a fixed amount, in a known currency, equal to it; one finding per run listing the count and the first five products; products whose prices differ are price-mismatch, not this
done: One system owns each price and the other reads it.
estimateChanges: The number of products, and code on both sides that has to change to read instead of store.

title: A subscription price in checkout has no plan on the page
what: A Stripe product you listed as a plan has an active subscription price that no plan on the page stands for.
why: A price that is live in Stripe but never shown is either a plan you forgot to put on the site, or an old price that can still be bought from an old link.
fix: Add the plan to the page, or archive the price in Stripe if it should no longer be sold.
tech: for each Stripe product in gaugeline.plans.json products (active), its prices with active true and a recurring object that no plan on the page was matched to; one finding per product listing up to three prices; a product that is archived, or not among the products that were read, says nothing here
done: The plan is on the page, or its price is archived in Stripe.
estimateChanges: Page design for the plan if it is shown for the first time.

title: A field your query asks for is missing on some documents
what: A query asks for a field that some published documents of the type have and others do not.
why: Fine when the field is optional. When the page assumes it is there (a link built from it, an image with no fallback), the documents without it break or show a gap.
fix: If the field is optional, make the template cope with it missing. If it is not, fill it in on the documents listed by their count, or mark it required in the schema.
tech: one GET of the query endpoint for each document type (perspective=published, so drafts are never counted), asking for count(*[_type == T]) and count(*[_type == T && defined(path)]) for each distinct field path, held in a Map from type to a Map from path to an integer; a reference or an array of objects is counted at the field itself (topic, not topic->title); the answer is integers, so no document and no field value is read; a path whose count is above 0 and below the type's total
done: The template copes with the field being missing, or every document has it, or the field is marked required.
estimateChanges: Filling in many documents is a data job. A template change is one edit.

title: A document has no stated total
what: A document of the type has no stated total at the field the rule names, so there is nothing to compare its parts with.
why: Either the pipeline skipped the field or the field was renamed. It is not a mismatch, because nothing was promised, but a page that prints the total prints a blank.
fix: Open the document by its id and fill the stated field in, or check the field name in the rule against your schema.
tech: one GET of the query endpoint for each rule (perspective=published, so drafts are never read); the filter does the comparing, so only ids and whole numbers come back, never a stated number, a part or any other field: the type's document count, the _id of the documents that have no stated number, and the _id of those where stated != coalesce(math::sum(parts), 0); a part that does not dereference is null and math::sum skips it; exact equality on the numbers, and the stated field or a part that is not a number on some document is exit 2 and nothing is reported; !defined(stated)
done: The stated field is filled in on each document named, or the rule's field name is corrected.
estimateChanges: Many documents are filled in one by one unless a migration sets them.
